source: We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely.
claim: The Transformer relies only on attention mechanisms and removes recurrence and convolution.
justification: This is a direct paraphrase of the abstract sentence about the architecture.

source: The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks in an encoder-decoder configuration. We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely.
claim: The dominant sequence transduction models use recurrent and convolutional neural networks, while the Transformer keeps those components.
justification: The excerpt explicitly says the older models are recurrent/convolutional and the Transformer dispenses with them; the claim reverses that statement.

source: Experiments on two machine translation tasks show these models to be superior in quality while being more parallelizable and requiring significantly less time to train.
claim: The Transformer is the best architecture for every NLP task.
justification: The excerpt reports two translation tasks only, not universal superiority across all NLP tasks.

source: We show that the Transformer generalizes well to other tasks by applying it successfully to English constituency parsing both with large and limited training data.
claim: The Transformer works equally well on every language task and dataset size.
justification: The excerpt says it generalizes well to other tasks and parsing, not that performance is equal across every task or dataset regime.

paper_title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
source: We introduce a new language representation model called BERT, which stands for Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers. Unlike recent language representation models, BERT is designed to pre-train deep bidirectional representations from unlabeled text by jointly conditioning on both left and right context in all layers.
claim: BERT is pretrained to condition on both left and right context in all layers.
justification: This closely restates the abstract sentence describing BERT’s bidirectional pretraining.

paper_title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
source: Unlike recent language representation models, BERT is designed to pre-train deep bidirectional representations from unlabeled text by jointly conditioning on both left and right context in all layers.
claim: BERT is a unidirectional language model trained only on left-to-right context.
justification: The excerpt explicitly says BERT is bidirectional and conditions on both left and right context, which directly contradicts the claim.

paper_title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
source: BERT is conceptually simple and empirically powerful. It obtains new state-of-the-art results on eleven natural language processing tasks, including pushing the GLUE score to 80.5% (7.7% point absolute improvement), MultiNLI accuracy to 86.7% (4.6% absolute improvement), SQuAD v1.1 question answering Test F1 to 93.2 (1.5 point absolute improvement) and SQuAD v2.0 Test F1 to 83.1 (5.1 point absolute improvement).
claim: BERT is the best model for every NLP task and every benchmark.
justification: The excerpt supports strong results on eleven tasks, not universal dominance on every NLP benchmark or task.
